reason: The text explicitly identifies the Hebrews as 'עַמִּ֖י' (ammi - 'my people') and 'בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל' (beney Yisrael - 'children/sons of Israel'), using corporate and national terminology rather than familial or purely religious designations. The passage portrays them as a distinct political entity enslaved under the Pharaoh of Egypt, organized enough to have elders ('זִקְנֵ֣י'), and separate from other nations (Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, etc.). While their covenantal relationship with Yahweh is emphasized throughout, the text primarily frames the Israelites as an oppressed people and nation requiring liberation from foreign rule, demonstrating national/political identity beyond merely being followers of God or members of an extended family.
story: Moses meets Yahweh in the Burning Bush
